title: Liberation on Broadway #liberationbroadway #liberationbway #besswohl ...
transcript: Liberation is a new play by Bess Wohl, now on Broadway following an acclaimed premiere earlier this year. It's a memory play about our narrator's mother Lizzie and her friends in Ohio in the 70s during the women's liberation movement. It's acknowledged at the top of the play that it's easy right now to feel like things are going in the wrong direction, so where did things go wrong? Jumping back and forth between today's point of view and the 70s, we see the evolution of six women from the formation of their CR group to a pivotal moment in Lizzie's life. As far as comparisons to when it was off-Broadway, it feels tighter now, but the dialogue remains strong, as does the direction by Whitney White. Tt's a lovely showcase of ensemble work and a complex but very engaging piece. I do struggle with some of the framing devices that are used throughout the play, and some of the commentary that brings a self-awareness that doesn't really do anything for me dramatically. For example, the play is very wide in scope and it raises questions that no two and a half hour play could sufficiently address. And even though it acknowledges this, I don't feel like that absolves it of any responsibility for those loose ends, and I would have preferred for it to have a sharper focus instead. Regardless, I think this play will resonate with a lot of people and there's plenty to appreciate here, especially in the performances. I think Betsy Aidem is giving a notably humorous and heartbreaking performance, but everyone in this eight person ensemble is great, and they all breathe a deep sense of humanity into this piece. Liberation is running now at the James Earl Jones Theatre on Broadway. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
